data.name: Ktrl Smash
data.detailed_description:
Ktrl Smash is a chaotic and fast-paced multiplayer arena brawler where every second counts. Jump into a bright 3D arena, choose your fighter, and battle players from around the world in short, intense matches. Your goal is simple: get the most kills before the timer hits zero.

The arena is packed with weapons and stat boosts, turning every match into a wild scramble. Pick up anything you can find, swing a baseball bat, throw a baseball, or smash someone with a chair. Each weapon changes how you fight, letting you surprise opponents or rush straight into the action.

Scattered around the map are useful pickups like Speed Boost, Damage Boost, and Health Boost. Grabbing them at the right moment can help you survive longer, strike faster, or turn a losing fight around. With players racing toward the same boosts, every pickup becomes a small battle of its own.

Matches are quick, lively, and unpredictable. One moment you are chasing someone with a bat, the next, you’re scrambling to grab a boost before someone else does. Simple controls make it easy to jump in, while the fast pace keeps every round exciting and competitive.

When the timer runs out, the player with the highest kills claims the win and becomes the ultimate champion.

data.short_description: Ktrl Smash is a fast-paced multiplayer arena game where anything can become a weapon. Pick your fighter, grab bats, baseballs, or even chairs, collect stat boosts, and fight to get the most kills before time runs out. Stay alert, keep moving, and defeat as many players as you can.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS: Windows 10 64Bit
  • Processor: Intel Core i3-4130 / AMD FX-8350
  • Memory: 4 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GTX 750 Ti / AMD Radeon R7 260X
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Network: Broadband Internet connection
  • Storage: 250 MB available space
  • Additional Notes: Designed for low-poly 3D visuals. Performance may vary in large multiplayer sessions.
